history.title: CI Gate Accuracy Interval Tolerance

style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist studio composition of a modular mechanical assembly on a brushed steel surface. A precision anodized aluminum inspection gauge featuring two narrow measuring brackets clasps a central machined test block, but the block's wider stepped base visibly extends beyond the restrictive brackets. Hard clean edges, one directional key light throwing a long cast shadow across the weathered steel, matte muted palette of industrial grey and safety orange. Generous negative space, extreme asymmetrical off-center composition. No bare shapes, no text, no molded or printed lettering.
negative_prompt: text, letters, numbers, watermark, garbled typography, labels, UI
rationale: The story is about a single numerical gate and its failure to measure true variance. Component assembly perfectly abstracts this statistical bottleneck into a tangible physical inspection tool that visibly misses the mark.
cue: wider bars than the benchmark number
subject: precision inspection gauge with brackets too narrow for its test block
core_thesis: A 100-case evaluation suite's claimed 95% accuracy interval only delivers 92.5% true coverage, providing falsely narrow error bars for ship-or-hold release gates.
core_conflict: Narrow benchmark accuracy vs wider generalized real-world performance variance
